hot.title: Language model harnesses are compositional generalizers
LLM-as-a-Coach: Experiential Learning for Non-Verifiable Tasks
hot.summary: Experiential Learning (EL), developed by Microsoft Research and collaborators, introduces an "LLM-as-a-Coach" framework that transforms rich textual feedback into high-bandwidth learning signals for post-training language models on non-verifiable, open-ended tasks. This method consistently outperformed traditional reinforcement learning, demonstrating improved generalization and reduced reward hacking on various open-ended benchmarks.

hot.title: Masked Visual Actions for Unified World Modeling
hot.summary: Researchers from Stanford University and collaborators developed Masked Visual Actions (MVA), a pixel-space control interface that enables a single pre-trained video model to function as a unified world model for both forward and inverse dynamics in robot manipulation. This approach achieved superior visual fidelity and cross-embodiment generalization in controllable video generation, improved planning success rates by up to 26% on Robocasa tasks, and demonstrated zero-shot inverse modeling with 90% success on a complex pick-and-place task.

hot.title: Exploration Matters for Escaping the Blur Trap in 3D Gaussian Splatting
hot.summary: Researchers from Hunan University and Nanyang Technological University identified the "Blur Trap" in 3D Gaussian Splatting, a persistent blur caused by biased gradient optimization, and introduced two minimal exploration operators—Random Seeding and Random Splitting—that significantly enhance scene detail and fidelity across diverse datasets.

hot.title: Mage-Flow: An Efficient Native-Resolution Foundation Model for Image Generation and Editing
hot.summary: Mage-Flow, a 4-billion-parameter foundation model, achieves competitive text-to-image generation and instruction-based image editing performance against significantly larger models. It demonstrates substantially faster inference (0.59s for 1024x1024 image generation) and lower memory usage (17.68 GB peak GPU memory for generation) on a single GPU through system-level co-design and an efficient latent tokenizer.

hot.title: RynnBrain 1.1: Towards More Capable and Generalizable Embodied Foundation Model
hot.summary: RynnBrain 1.1, an upgraded family of embodied foundation models from DAMO Academy, Alibaba Group, and Hupan Lab, enhances physical world understanding and generalizability for robot control. It achieves precise 3D grounding and contact point prediction capabilities, leading to significantly improved real-robot manipulation performance across diverse platforms compared to previous models.

hot.title: Patch Policy: Efficient Embodied Control via Dense Visual Representations
hot.summary: The researchers developed PATCH POLICY, an efficient, modular Transformer-based policy that directly utilizes dense visual representations from frozen, pre-trained Vision Transformers. This approach achieves superior performance in precise robot manipulation tasks with significantly reduced computational cost and faster inference compared to large Vision-Language-Action models.

hot.title: FlowMimic: Mask-free Visual Editing and Generation with Pixel-pair Warped Flow Field for Online Video Editing Data Generation and Modality Mimicry
hot.summary: FlowMimic introduces a framework for generating video editing training data in real-time from image editing samples, using a pixel-pair warped flow field to overcome limitations in traditional data collection. The method aligns image and video modalities and internalizes language-visual understanding for mask-free editing, showcasing broad generalization across various video editing and generation tasks.

hot.title: SWE-Pruner Pro: The Coder LLM Already Knows What to Prune
hot.summary: SWE-Pruner Pro enables large language model (LLM) coding agents to perform context pruning by leveraging the LLM's internal representations for per-line keep-or-prune decisions on tool outputs. This approach significantly reduces token consumption, with up to 39% savings, and often enhances task performance, such as increasing the SWE-Bench Verified resolve rate by 3.8% with MiMo-V2-Flash, while incurring minimal additional overhead.

hot.title: ABot-World-0: Infinite Interactive World Rollout on a Single Desktop GPU
Introducing Laguna S 2.1
FM-VLA: Force-based Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models in Contact-Rich Manipulation
hot.summary: FM-VLA enhances Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models with a novel force-based memory for long-horizon temporal reasoning in contact-rich manipulation tasks. The model achieved an average success rate of 83.3% across challenging memory-dependent tasks, outperforming existing baselines, while adding minimal inference latency.

hot.title: TimeLens2: Generalist Video Temporal Grounding with Multimodal LLMs
hot.summary: A research team from Nanjing University and Shanghai AI Laboratory developed TimeLens2, a generalist Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) designed for video temporal grounding, capable of precisely localizing single and multi-interval evidence within long videos across diverse domains and query types. This MLLM sets a new benchmark in performance across seven temporal grounding datasets, outperforming larger existing models through its novel data construction pipeline and a temporal Wasserstein reward for training.

hot.title: Agentic Real2Sim: Physics-based World Modeling with Vision-Language Agents
hot.summary: Agentic Real2Sim is a framework that automates the conversion of real-world robotic interaction videos into physically simulatable digital twins. It successfully reconstructs DROID rigid manipulation episodes into MuJoCo, achieving 48% replay success, and extends qualitatively to deformable and humanoid interactions.

hot.title: Pixel-Space Diffusion Transformers
hot.summary: Pixel-Space Diffusion Transformers (pDiTs) are presented as a re-emerging paradigm for high-fidelity visual synthesis, directly modeling raw pixels to overcome the information bottleneck of latent diffusion models. The work surveys their architectural advancements, mathematical foundations, and role in developing unified multimodal AI, while detailing challenges and future directions.

hot.title: OmniReasoner: Thinking with Long Audio-Video via Native Tool Use
Automated Discovery Has No Universally Superior Harness
hot.summary: Research at UC Berkeley and MIT demonstrated that no single fixed harness consistently outperforms others in LLM-guided discovery systems across various models and problems. Instead, adaptive allocation strategies that prune less promising runs based on early progress consistently achieved higher average scores, ranging from 84.87% to 85.75%, surpassing non-adaptive baselines.

hot.title: WorldScape Policy 2.0: Empowering Steerable World Action Modeling with Reasoning-Augmented Memory
Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
hot.summary: Researchers from New York University and collaborators established a quantitative framework to understand the interplay between large language model pretraining and reinforcement learning in reasoning tasks, using a controlled chess environment. They developed a joint pretraining-RL scaling law, revealing that lower pretraining loss predicts higher post-RL performance and that optimal RL compute share increases with total compute, while also showing RL reshapes policies through both ground-truth amplification and wrong-mode amplification.

hot.title: Distilled Reinforcement Learning for LLM Post-training
hot.summary: The Distilled Reinforcement Learning (Distilled RL) framework integrates teacher knowledge directly into the reinforcement learning objective, providing fine-grained, selective guidance to large language models. This approach consistently outperforms existing RL and on-policy distillation methods, particularly in challenging cross-family distillation scenarios, by facilitating new knowledge acquisition and achieving sustained performance gains.

likes.title: Language model harnesses are compositional generalizers
SEED: Self-Evolving On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: SEED (SElf-Evolving On-Policy Distillation) enables large language model (LLM) agents to learn more effectively from their own experiences by generating and internalizing self-evolving, on-policy hindsight skills. This framework achieves substantial performance gains, such as a 14.9 to 45.9 percentage point improvement in macro-average success rate over outcome-only reinforcement learning on ALFWorld, through dense, token-level supervision and enhanced sample efficiency.

likes.title: On-Policy Delta Distillation
likes.summary: Researchers from NAVER AI Lab introduce On-Policy Delta Distillation (OPD^2), a method for post-training large language models that isolates and distills the specific reasoning capabilities acquired by a teacher model. OPD^2 achieves superior performance over existing on-policy distillation methods across diverse reasoning tasks, model sizes, and generation modes, notably improving math reasoning for a 1.7B parameter model by nearly 20 percentage points.

likes.title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
likes.summary: Researchers from New York University and collaborators established a quantitative framework to understand the interplay between large language model pretraining and reinforcement learning in reasoning tasks, using a controlled chess environment. They developed a joint pretraining-RL scaling law, revealing that lower pretraining loss predicts higher post-RL performance and that optimal RL compute share increases with total compute, while also showing RL reshapes policies through both ground-truth amplification and wrong-mode amplification.

likes.title: Video = World + Event Stream
likes.summary: The Wan Team, Alibaba Group, developed a "world + event stream" decomposition for video content, establishing a general-purpose pretraining approach for interactive AI. This method enables real-time agents to perform open-vocabulary, free-form behaviors synchronized with speech at 640x368 resolution and 25 FPS, while preserving a low model-side latency of approximately 200 ms.

likes.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
likes.summary: NVIDIA researchers introduced RoboTTT, a framework that leverages Test-Time Training (TTT) to extend visuomotor context in robot foundation models to 8,000 timesteps while maintaining constant inference latency. This approach enables robots to achieve superior performance on complex, long-horizon tasks and unlocks capabilities such as one-shot in-context imitation and improved robustness to perturbations.

likes.title: VideoChat3: Fully Open Video MLLM for Efficient and Generalist Video Understanding
likes.summary: VideoChat3 introduces a fully open and efficient Video Multimodal Large Language Model (Video MLLM) designed for generalist video understanding across diverse durations and interaction modes. The model achieves strong performance on various video benchmarks while providing substantial computational efficiency for long and streaming videos, with all training components publicly released.

likes.title: T^2MLR: Transformer with Temporal Middle-Layer Recurrence
likes.summary: Princeton Language and Intelligence researchers developed a Transformer with Temporal Middle-Layer Recurrence (T²MLR), integrating recurrence into the network's middle layers to overcome the token-centric information bottleneck in autoregressive decoding. This approach improves reasoning capabilities on tasks such as S5-Retrieval and math benchmarks, maintains efficient inference with approximately 8% overhead, and can be retrofitted into pretrained models, achieving up to 40.6% relative accuracy increase on MATH500.

likes.title: TRACE: Turn-level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation for Long-Horizon Agents
likes.summary: TRACE, developed by researchers from the University of Wisconsin–Madison and Microsoft Research, introduces a critic-free credit assignment method for long-horizon agentic tasks. It enhances multi-turn tool-use performance in large language models by deriving dense, turn-level rewards from a frozen reference model's gold-answer predictability, achieving accuracy increases from 7.2% to 35.6% for Qwen3-4B and faster learning on search benchmarks.

likes.title: GigaWorld-Policy-0.5: A Faster and Stronger WAM Empowered by AutoResearch
likes.summary: Researchers from GigaAI and Tsinghua University developed GigaWorld-Policy-0.5, a World Action Model that achieves real-time robotic control by decoupling future visual prediction from action inference. The system recorded an 85 ms inference latency on an edge GPU and demonstrated up to a 33% relative improvement in success rates on complex manipulation tasks compared to baseline models.

likes.title: Loop the Loopies!
likes.summary: A new scaling methodology, the "Loopie Recipe," enables recurrent Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models to achieve competitive or superior performance under identical pre-training compute budgets. This approach culminated in Loopie models demonstrating gold-medal level performance on the International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) and International Physics Olympiad (IPhO) 2025 problems without external tools.

likes.title: Scaling Behavior Foundation Model for Humanoid Robots
likes.summary: Researchers from Shanghai AI Lab and collaborating institutions systematically investigated the scaling of Behavior Foundation Models (BFMs) for humanoid robots, developing a principled recipe that integrates global-frame motion tracking, a balance of data quantity and diversity, and a Humanoid Transformer architecture. This approach led to a reduction in Mean Per-Keypoint Position Error (MPKPE) on the test set by over 10% in local mode and 82% in global mode compared to prior methods.

likes.title: xHC: Expanded Hyper-Connections
likes.summary: xHC, developed by researchers from Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Xiaohongshu Inc., enables effective and affordable expansion of multi-stream residual architectures in Large Language Models beyond previous N=4 limitations. It enhances information flow and reduces computational costs, resulting in improved pre-training loss and downstream task performance with less compute than prior methods.

likes.title: DriftWorld: Fast World Modeling through Drifting
likes.summary: DriftWorld introduces an action-conditioned world model that generates future robot interaction frames in a single forward pass, achieving up to 17x faster inference (30+ fps) than diffusion models while matching or exceeding their visual quality. This model significantly boosts policy improvement metrics and demonstrates high correlation (up to 0.99 Pearson r^2) for offline policy evaluation across various robotic tasks.

likes.title: MeanFlowNFT: Bringing Forward-Process RL to Average-Velocity Generators
Recursive Harness Self-Improvement
likes.summary: Sakana AI and UC Berkeley researchers developed Recursive Harness Self-Improvement (RHI), an iterative algorithm that refines user-constructed agent harnesses based on pairwise feedback from execution history. RHI enables low-reasoning-effort agents to outperform stronger baselines while reducing inference costs by up to 60%, demonstrating that effective task-specific context management via prompt-level specifications can significantly enhance AI system performance and efficiency.

likes.title: VideoRAE: Taming Video Foundation Models for Generative Modeling via Representation Autoencoders
likes.summary: A semantic-driven video autoencoder called VideoRAE leverages frozen Video Foundation Models (VFMs) to create robust latent spaces suitable for high-fidelity video generation. This approach achieves state-of-the-art class-conditional generation, with gFVD scores of 40 (discrete) and 93 (continuous) on UCF-101, while also accelerating generative model convergence by up to five times.

likes.title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
likes.summary: Researchers from the National University of Singapore and The Hong Kong Polytechnic University introduced BadWAM, a framework for "World-Action Drift Attacks" that desynchronize a robot's executed actions from its imagined future in World-Action Models (WAMs). This work demonstrates that WAMs can be manipulated to cause task failures even when their predicted future world states appear plausible, challenging the assumption that future prediction inherently guarantees safe behavior.

likes.title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
likes.summary: SearchOS-V1 introduces a system-level multi-agent framework for robust open-domain information-seeking, externalizing search state into explicit, shared components and employing pipeline-parallel scheduling. The system achieved the best overall F1 scores on WideSearch, improving by 4.3 points, and reduced average end-to-end search time by 24.3% through enhanced coordination and error handling.

likes.title: Xiaomi-Robotics-1: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with over 100K Hours of Real-World Trajectories
likes.summary: Xiaomi Robotics developed a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model by pre-training on over 100,000 hours of real-world manipulation trajectories collected via Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) devices and an automated language labeling pipeline. This approach enabled the model to demonstrate strong out-of-the-box generalization to novel environments and efficient adaptation to new tasks on various robot embodiments.
